chapter: New Orleans musicians, recordings and radio
title: Singing at the Hollywood Club with Elmer Snowden's band and Duke Ellington
summary: She sang at the Hollywood Club at 49th and Broadway, run by gangsters, with Snowden's band that included Duke; the club burned down while the band had been told to leave their instruments.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, I've heard -- musicians have told me, like Elmer Snowden -- I don't know if you know him.
Yes. Well, certainly I met -- when Duke Ellington came up from Washington, and Snowden was playing in Duke's band, Duke was playing in Snowden's band --
Right.
See? Duke was playing in Snowden's band. I sang with Duke right here at 49th and Broadway at the club called the Hollywood Club. And Duke was playing with Elmer Snowden's band.
Right.
And not Duke's.
And they came up here and starved for a few days.
Sure did.
(Bricktop inaudible) was the one that got them the job.
That's right, Hollywood Club, 49th and Broadway.
What was it like, the Hollywood Club?
Oh, it was lovely. They -- and they had -- they had a few nice -- few pretty chorus girls down there, and I don't remember who else. I think --
Now, that was gangster-run.
Oh, yeah, that was gangster-run.
I remember Elmer (Inaudible) told me --

And that was -- there was a Mr. Jerry Sullivan. He was supposed to be the manager. I don't know what Mr. Jerry was, but he was -- anyhow he was nice to us. They were all nice to us. And there's -- I'm trying -- Flo -- it wasn't Freddy and Flo, but the dancer was named Flo. And who else worked there that you'd like to know about? I don't know. Anyhow, I know Duke's band -- I mean Elmer Snowden's band was there.
Elmer told me that one night the boss came to him and said, look, when you leave tonight, tell the boys to take their instruments. And they didn't.
Uh-huh, and when they came back --
It was burned down during the night.
That's right. That was right.
And Elmer was playing saxophone in those days, also.
Uh-huh, that's right. Yeah, now let me see what else happened. I'm trying to think about --
